title: "Metabolomics QC for the pre-specified contrasts"
author: "Jannik Franken"

  html_document:
    toc: true

## Purpose

Before any differential analysis, check for each pre-specified contrast (D22)
which lines enter the model, how the groups fall across tissues and culture
batches, whether the design is estimable, and how much of the metabolic
variation follows tissue, batch and the mutation group. A mutation group that
lines up with one batch or one tissue could not be separated from it.

**Decision supported:** whether the designs agreed at Checkpoint 2 can be
fitted as specified (Phase 4).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds`
- `config.yml`: `contrast` (gene roles, groups, minimum sizes), `differential.contrasts`

## Methods

For each contrast, lines were selected with `contrast_lines()` (lines used in
models, tissues of the contrast, known group status; with tissue blocking only
tissues with at least two altered and two unaltered lines) and the design
`~ batch + tissue + blocking + covariates + group` (blocking: histology in the
lung contrasts, D28) was built with `contrast_design()`;
terms that do not vary among the lines are left out. Balance of the group
across batches was tested with Fisher's exact test (simulated p-value). A PCA
was computed on the log2 values of the contrast's lines, each ion centred and
scaled; for the first five components, the share of variance explained by
tissue, batch and group was taken as the R² of a linear model of the component
on each factor alone.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/differential.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
output_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "04_metabolomics_qc")
set.seed(config$contrast$seed)

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
contrasts <- config$differential$contrasts
names(contrasts)
```

## 1. Lines and designs

```{r designs}
# lines, design and balance per contrast
qc <- lapply(contrasts, function(contrast) {
    d <- contrast_lines(data, contrast, config)
    X <- contrast_design(d, c(contrast$blocking, contrast$covariates))
    list(d = d, X = X)
})

design_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(qc), function(id) {
    d <- qc[[id]]$d
    X <- qc[[id]]$X
    tibble(
        contrast = id,
        lines = nrow(d), altered = sum(d$group), unaltered = sum(!d$group),
        tissues = paste(sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", names(table(d$tissue)),
                                tapply(d$group, d$tissue, sum), tapply(!d$group, d$tissue, sum)), collapse = ", "),
        terms = paste(setdiff(colnames(X), "(Intercept)"), collapse = " + "),
        residual_df = nrow(X) - ncol(X),
        batch_balance_p = fisher.test(table(d$batch, d$group), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e4)$p.value
    )
}))
preview_table(design_summary, caption = "Lines and design per contrast (tissue: altered/unaltered)")
```

```{r batches-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
# altered and unaltered lines per batch
p <- bind_rows(lapply(names(qc), function(id) mutate(qc[[id]]$d, contrast = id))) %>%
    mutate(group = if_else(group, "altered", "unaltered")) %>%
    count(contrast, batch, group) %>%
    ggplot(aes(batch, n, fill = group)) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(~contrast, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(c("altered", "unaltered"))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Lines", fill = NULL, title = "Groups across culture batches") +
    theme_uc() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_figure(p, "groups_per_batch", output_dir, width = 9, height = 5)
p
```

Covariate status within the groups, so that a covariate that almost
coincides with the group is visible:

```{r covariates}
bind_rows(lapply(names(qc), function(id) {
    d <- qc[[id]]$d
    covs <- contrasts[[id]]$covariates
    tibble(contrast = id, covariate = covs,
           share_in_altered = sapply(covs, function(cv) mean(d[[cv]][d$group])),
           share_in_unaltered = sapply(covs, function(cv) mean(d[[cv]][!d$group])))
})) %>%
    mutate(across(starts_with("share"), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```

## 2. Variance explained by tissue, batch and group

```{r pca}
# PCA of the contrast's lines; R2 of each factor alone on PC1-5
pca_of <- function(d) {
    pc <- prcomp(data$log2[d$line, ], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
    scores <- as_tibble(pc$x[, 1:5]) %>% mutate(line = d$line) %>% left_join(d, by = "line")
    share <- (pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2))[1:5]
    r2 <- expand_grid(pc = paste0("PC", 1:5), factor = c("tissue", "batch", "group")) %>%
        rowwise() %>%
        mutate(r2 = if (n_distinct(scores[[factor]]) > 1)
            summary(lm(scores[[pc]] ~ factor(scores[[factor]])))$r.squared else NA_real_) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(variance_share = share[as.integer(sub("PC", "", pc))])
    list(scores = scores, r2 = r2, share = share)
}
pcas <- lapply(qc, function(x) pca_of(x$d))

r2_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pcas), function(id) mutate(pcas[[id]]$r2, contrast = id)))
r2_table %>%
    mutate(r2 = round(r2, 2), variance_share = round(variance_share, 3)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = factor, values_from = r2) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "R² of tissue, batch and group on the first five components")
```

```{r pca-r2-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
# tissue is constant in the lung-only contrasts and has no R²
p <- ggplot(filter(r2_table, !is.na(r2)), aes(pc, r2, fill = factor)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    facet_wrap(~contrast) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(c("tissue", "batch", "group"))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "R² (factor alone)", fill = NULL,
         title = "Variance of the leading components explained by each factor") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "pca_r2", output_dir, width = 9, height = 5)
p
```

```{r pca-plots, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
# PC1/PC2 per contrast, coloured by group, shaped by batch
p <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pcas), function(id) mutate(pcas[[id]]$scores, contrast = id))) %>%
    mutate(group = if_else(group, "altered", "unaltered")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = group)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~contrast, scales = "free") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = uc_palette(c("altered", "unaltered"))) +
    labs(colour = NULL, title = "PCA of the lines of each contrast") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "pca", output_dir, width = 10, height = 8)
p
```

## Interpretation

- **All four designs are estimable** with the specified terms and leave 70–107
  residual degrees of freedom. In the lung-only contrasts the tissue term drops
  out because there is only one tissue, and histology blocks instead (D28).
- **Group sizes:** NRF2 in lung 24/61, KRAS 30/66 (lung, colon, blood), MTAP
  deletion 32/89 (six tissues, lines with copy number), STK11 in lung 22/63.
- **No group lines up with a culture batch** (Fisher p 0.07–0.60). The NRF2
  group comes closest (p = 0.07), and batch is in every model.
- **Batch is the largest visible factor:** it explains about a third of PC2
  (R² 0.31–0.37) and a fifth of PC5 in every contrast, while the mutation
  group explains at most 0.12 of any leading component. This supports keeping
  batch in the model (D8) and shows that mutation effects, if present, are
  not the dominant source of variation; they have to be found ion by ion.
- **Co-mutations within the lung contrasts are as expected:** STK11 and the
  NRF2 group co-occur (STK11 in 42 % of NRF2-altered vs 20 % of other lung
  lines; KEAP1 in 45 % of STK11-altered vs 14 %), and KRAS-mutant lines carry
  fewer TP53 alterations. These genes are covariates in the respective models,
  so their effects are not attributed to the group.
